problems.title: Range of a combined exponential
problems.question: Find the range of $4^x2^{1+x^2}$.
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
steps: The exponent ranges over[0,∞). Since base 2 is increasing, the range starts at 2⁰=1 and is unbounded.

problems.title: A logarithmic inequality with decreasing base
problems.question: Find the smallest integer satisfying $\log_{0.5}(2x+9)\le\log_{0.5}(7-2x)$.
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: The domain is −9/2<x<7/2. Because the base is below 1, the inequality reverses: $2x+9\ge7-2x$.
steps: This gives x≥−1/2. The solution is[−1/2,7/2), whose smallest integer is 0.

problems.title: Reciprocal bases in a strict inequality
problems.question: Solve $(2-\sqrt3)^x<(2+\sqrt3)^2$.
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: The bases multiply to 1. With t=2+√3>1, the inequality is $t^{-x}<t^2$.
steps: Compare exponents:−x<2.

problems.title: Volume of a square frustum
problems.question: A regular square frustum has space diagonal 9 and base sides 5,7. Find its volume.
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: The space diagonal’s horizontal projection has offsets 6,6, so $h^2=9^2-6^2-6^2=9$.
steps: h=3. The frustum volume is(h/3)(S₁+√(S₁S₂)+S₂)=(3/3)(25+35+49).

problems.title: Largest ball carved from a cylinder
problems.question: A cylinder has height 20 and radius 9. What fraction of its volume is the largest ball that fits inside it?
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: The ball radius is $\min(9,20/2)=9$. Sphere volume is 4πr³/3 and cylinder volumeπ·9²·20.

problems.title: A product of logarithms
problems.question: Solve $\sqrt{x+7}>\log_35\log_527$.
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: The logarithm product is $\log_327=3$.
steps: The radical inequality becomes √(x+7)>3. Squaring gives x+7>9, and this already meets the radical domain.

problems.title: Largest integer exponential solution
problems.question: Find the largest integer satisfying $2^{2x}-3\cdot2^x+2\le0$.
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: Set t=2ˣ>0. The inequality factors as $(t-1)(t-2)\le0$.
steps: Thus 1≤2ˣ≤2, so 0≤x≤1. The largest integer is 1.

problems.title: A radical exponent and reciprocal logarithmic bases
problems.question: Solve $(\log_72)^{\sqrt{x^2}-1}>(\log_27)^{x-1}$.
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: Let c=log₇2∈(0,1); then log₂7=1/c and √x²=|x|. The inequality is $c^{|x|-1}>c^{1-x}$.
steps: Since 0<c<1, compare exponents in reverse order:|x|−1<1−x, or|x|+x<2. For x≤0 this always holds; for x>0 it gives x<1.

problems.title: Sphere inside a cone frustum
problems.question: A sphere is inscribed in a cone frustum with base radii 4,9. Find its radius.
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: Tangency in the axial trapezoid gives sphere-radius squared $\rho^2=Rr$.

problems.title: Sphere tangent to all rhombus sides
problems.question: A rhombus has diagonals 15,20. A ball of volume 4000π/3 touches all four sides. Find its centre’s distance from the rhombus plane.
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: The ball radius is 10 from $4\pi R^3/3=4000\pi/3$. The rhombus are a is 150, side 12.5, semiperimeter 25, so its inradius is 6.
steps: The plane section is the rhombus incircle. Thus the plane distance d satisfies d²+6²=10², giving d=8.

problems.title: An exponential and logarithmic system
problems.question: Solve $5^{x^2+5x}>5^{30-2x}$ and $\log_5(x+12)>1$.
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: The first inequality is $x^2+7x-30=(x+10)(x-3)>0$. The second gives x+12>5, or x>−7.
steps: Intersect x<−10 or x>3 with x>−7.

problems.title: A chain of logarithms
problems.question: Solve $\log_3\sqrt[3]3\cdot\log_{\sqrt[3]3}(x-1)<0$.
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: The product is $\log_3(x-1)$ by change of base. Its domain is x>1.
steps: Base 3 is increasing, so the logarithm is negative precisely for 0<x−1<1.

problems.title: An exponential graph missing only quadrant I
problems.question: The graph y=a·199ˣ+b passes through every quadrant except I. Which listed sign condition must hold?
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: As x→−∞, y→b. To reach quadrant II requires b>0. To keep the right-hand side x>0 out of quadrant I while reaching IV requires a<0.
steps: Moreover crossing into quadrant III requires a+b<0, placing the x-intercept on the negative x-axis. Among the printed sign choices, the necessary one is a<0, b>0.
problems.answer: a<0, b>0 (with a+b<0 for the full stated quadrant pattern).

problems.title: Volume ratio from three edge fractions
problems.question: In tetrahedron MABC, E, F, K lie on MA, MC, MB with ME: EA=1:2, MF: FC=3:1, MK=KB. Find V(MKEF)/V(MABC).
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: The volume scales by the product of the three fractions along the edges from M.
steps: The fractions are 1/3,3/4,1/2. Their product is 1/8.

problems.title: A cube inside a hemisphere
problems.question: A cube of side 4 has its lower four vertices on a hemisphere’s base plane and its upper four on its surface. Find the volume of the full sphere.
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: The sphere centre is the centre of the lower square. A radius to a top corner has offsets 2,2,4, so $R^2=4+4+16=24$.
steps: R=2√6. The full ball volume is 4πR³/3=(4π/3)(48√6).

problems.title: A parameter forced negative
problems.question: If $4^a-3\cdot49^a+2\cdot14^a>0$, which listed claim must hold?
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: Divide by 49ᵃ>0 and set $t=(2/7)^a>0$. The inequality becomes $t^2+2t-3=(t-1)(t+3)>0$.
steps: Thus t>1. Since 2/7<1, this forces a<0. Therefore the necessary listed equality is |a|=−a.

problems.title: An empty logarithmic-power root set
problems.question: Which of the four printed finite sets contain every solution of $x^{\log_5x}=1/625$?
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: Domain x>0. Let t=log₅x. Then $x^{\log_5x}=5^{t^2}\ge1$, while 1/625<1.
steps: There are no real solutions. The empty set is a subset of each of the four printed sets.
problems.answer: All four sets A, B, C, D.

problems.title: Infer the logarithm base from one solution
problems.question: Solve $\log_a(2x^2-3x+1)<\log_a(x-1)$, given x=2 satisfies it.
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: At x=2, the inequality is logₐ3<logₐ1=0, forcing 0<a<1. The domain reduces to x>1.
steps: For this decreasing logarithm, reverse the argument comparison:2x²−3x+1>x−1. This is 2(x−1)²>0, which holds for every x>1.

problems.title: A sphere from two perpendicular circular sections
problems.question: Two radius 5 circles on a sphere share a chord 2√2 long. Their planes are perpendicular. Find ball volume.
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: Let h be the sphere centre’s distance to each section plane and R its radius. Equal circle radii imply equal plane distances. Then $R^2-h^2=25$ and $R^2-2h^2=(\sqrt2)^2=2$.
steps: Subtract to obtain h²=23, R²=48, so R=4√3. Volume 4πR³/3=256√3π.

problems.title: Cylinder volume from an inclined chord section
problems.question: A plane through the lower base centre of a cylinder makes angle α with the base and cuts a chord b in the upper circle, subtending arc β. tanα=3√3, b=4, cot(β/2)=2. Find volume.
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: The chord half-length is 2, so its offset d from the upper centre is $2\cot(\beta/2)=4$. The radius satisfies $R^2=d^2+2^2=20$.
steps: The plane’s slope gives h=d tanα=12√3. Thus V=πR²h=240√3π.

problems.title: Nested logarithms of reciprocal arguments
problems.question: Which listed x satisfies $\log_3\log_4((4x-1)/(x+1))-\log_{1/3}\log_{1/4}((x+1)/(4x-1))<0$?
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: Put t=(4x−1)/(x+1). The inner logarithms are equal: $\log_{1/4}(1/t)=\log_4t=u$. The expression is 2log₃u.
steps: Its negativity and domain require 0<u<1, or 1<t<4. Since t=4−5/(x+1), these conditions reduce to x>2/3. Among 7/25,1/8,1/5,3/5,5/8,7/8, only 7/8 qualifies.

problems.title: A whole solution set satisfies another inequality
problems.question: Which printed interval consists entirely of a values such that every solution of x²≤a also satisfies(a−3x)√(x+5)≥0?
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: For a<0, the first solution set is empty, so the implication is vacuous. At a=0, the only root 0 works. For a>0, it is[−√a,√a].
steps: This interval lies in the radical domain only if a≤25. Its most restrictive value for a−3x is x=√a, requiring a−3√a≥0, or a≥9. Thus the full parameter set is(−∞,0]∪[9,25].
Of the printed intervals, only(11,21) lies wholly inside this set.

problems.title: An exponential inequality with no solutions
problems.question: Which listed interval consists entirely of a values for which 25ˣ−a5ˣ+3−a≤0 has no solution?
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: Put t=5ˣ>0. The polynomial is $t^2-at+3-a$. For a≤0 it is positive for every t>0.
steps: For a>0 its minimum on t>0 is 3−a−a²/4, which is positive precisely when a<2. At a=2 the minimum 0 is attained; for larger a there is a nonpositive value. Thus no solutions exactly when a<2. Of the printed intervals, only(−9,1) is entirely below 2.

problems.title: An insphere volume determines a cone angle
problems.question: A cone contains an inscribed ball whose volume is one third the product of cone base are a and ball radius. Find the cosine of the cone’s axial apex angle.
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: $4\pi r^3/3=\pi R^2r/3$ gives r=R/2. For half-apex angle θ, the axial-triangle inradius relation is $r/R=\cos\theta/(1+\sin\theta)$.
steps: Thus cosθ=(1+sinθ)/2. Squaring and putting s=sinθ gives 5s²+2s−3=0. The valid positive root is 3/5. Therefore the apex-angle cosine is cos 2θ=1−2s²=1−18/25.

problems.title: Pyramid volume from a circumsphere
problems.question: A pyramid has equilateral base side 12 and one lateral edge perpendicular to the base. Its circumsphere radius is 8. Find volume.
problems.idea: Use exact base changes, domains, and geometric relations.
formulas: The base circumradius is $12/\sqrt3=4\sqrt3$. The sphere centre lies over the base circumcentre. Equal distances to the perpendicular edge’s endpoints put its height at h/2.
steps: Thus 8²=(4√3)²+h²/4, so h=8. Base are a is 12²√3/4=36√3. Volume=base are a·h/3.
